findings.evidence: Lines 71–90 expose the mapped-list-product body while immediately providing equations sufficient for ordinary evaluation and composition.
findings.fix: Remove `@[expose]`; retain the body-independent equations as the public API.
findings.issue: `wordProd` is marked `@[expose]` even though `wordProd_nil`, `wordProd_cons`, and `wordProd_append` provide an unfolding-free interface.

findings.evidence: Mathlib/GroupTheory/Coxeter/Basic.lean:374 and :380 expose exactly `wordProd_singleton` and `wordProd_reverse` for the parallel Coxeter word API.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp] wordProd_singleton` and `@[simp] wordProd_reverse`; prove them using the existing nil/cons/append API and `ofIdx_inv`.
findings.issue: The public word operation lacks the standard singleton and reverse/inverse equations, forcing consumers to reconstruct basic behavior from implementation lemmas.

findings.evidence: Line 87 states `(weylGroup.ofIdx P i)⁻¹ = weylGroup.ofIdx P i`; this is terminating and strictly removes an inverse.
findings.fix: Annotate `ofIdx_inv` with `@[simp]` so inverses of simple reflections normalize automatically.
findings.issue: The newly public `ofIdx_inv` is a canonical normal-form rule but is not tagged `@[simp]`.

summary: The public word-product API unnecessarily exposes its implementation and omits standard characteristic lemmas; the newly public involution identity also lacks its canonical simplification annotation.
